independent_controls.method: Independent scalar Python transcription of inspected resize/hash formulas. NOT original Lisp execution, independent Imago normalization, or image decoder validation.

conclusions: Implementation computes 1024-bit aHash and two-neighbour dHash. dHash samples a 33x33 thumbnail and compares twice current intensity to right plus below; offsets are consistent with 33-wide row stride.

Resize bins every input pixel into one output cell, averages integers and uses max(1,count), leaving empty output cells zero. Source explicitly documents dimensions below target as unsupported quality.
Independent model: uniform white 1x1 and 32x32 yield aHash Hamming distance 1023/1024 due to empty cells. This characterizes inspected formulas, not original Lisp runtime behavior.

Independent positive controls preserve constant intensity when both dimensions reach target; uniform black/white at target dimensions share both modeled signatures. No exact identity should follow from hash equality.

Two upstream FiveAM tests each call a common helper: different image pair and two perturbations on each of two images. Threshold 30 versus README example45; perturbations include 50 random black-pixel writes without fixed seed. Original tests not executed.

Imago grayscale/decoder extensions own color conversion. Changelog 0.3.1 requires loading decoder extensions explicitly; project itself depends on core Imago while tests add imago/jpeg-turbo. ICC, alpha, EXIF and format claims not independently qualified.
Both original JPEGs viewed: distinct illustrated portraits; no real-photo or difficult-transform corpus. Lock records Quicklisp distributions, not byte-level checksums of dependency sources.
Original CI downloads Roswell installer and runs qlot tests on Ubuntu. No Lisp implementation found on current PATH; no install, CI script, decoder or upstream test executed.
license: Root BSD-2-Clause fully read; no production source adopted.
limits: Full source/fixture review with three independent formula controls does not establish original runtime, image quality, format coverage, platform parity or performance.
